rotation.topic: Bypassing Safety Controls · Stop Work Authority

openingMessage: Today we own our day before it owns us. Every crew out there is counting on the person next to them. Let's make sure we're worth counting on.
openingWhy: Odessa, 2019. A pumper answered a routine pump alarm at a waterflood station without his H2S monitor on. The gas dropped him at the site — and when he didn't come home, his wife drove out looking for him. It got her too. The people counting on your discipline today aren't all on location. Some of them are at home.
leadershipThought: Before you leave today: What is one thing I can improve before I drive away? Not because someone is watching. Because excellence is a habit. And habits become character.

specialFocus.title: Finish Strong — The Week Stop Work Got Written Down
specialFocus.why: Last day of the work week, so we finish it the way we started it: with excellence. Jacob's week on Bypassing Safety Controls and Stop Work Authority opened Monday with a hard number. Last week we made at least 13 real stops and wrote almost none of them down well enough for anyone to picture them. So Monday we set the standard: make the call, then paint the scene. Tuesday we ran it back and helped each other out the door. Wednesday we heard the names behind the catches. And this week the field answered. The notes that came in look different. They have times, readings and the moves the crew made, written down while the scene was fresh. That's the standard showing up on location, not just on the board. This morning we name it, lock it in, and go finish the week clean.
specialFocus.standardLabel: What Excellence Looked Like This Week
standard: The note we were looking for. Tuesday at Brook N-13D 100H, Bryan Medlin wrote: 'While disconnecting flow line at 9:38 we encountered LEL's at 4 ppm. Stopped the job, shut all machines off till the air cleared, at 9:43 went to check air quality and found nothing leaking or contaminants in the air. Proceeded with disconnecting flow line.' The time, the reading, the stop, what he did, the recheck and how it ended are all there. Anyone could picture that location from his words. The office review wants to use it as the example for the whole crew.

A safety control held, not bypassed. Wednesday at Pintail O 31-30 2815H, the crew was about to grab the impact wrench. Bobby Galindo stopped them, because LEL was reading around 17 in that spot, and had them finish with hand tools and a brass hammer. That is this week's topic in one move. When the condition says the normal way isn't safe, you don't push through it. You change the method and keep the control in place.

Paperwork that tells the truth. Luis Zarate's XBC Giddings air job carried the most complete OWL close-out of Wednesday. Raymundo Solis filed a filled-in Learn section, and Baldemar Bracamontes a full observe list with a real narrative. Joseph Popillion paused and closed his flowback job correctly over four days, with the suspended time recorded right. Nathan Contreras, Jerry Gonzales, Jordan Lemmons and Bryan Medlin turned in complete trailer paperwork. Larry Taylor and Rolando Flores filed clean dailies.

Help each other, all week long. Remember Tuesday's twist: quick but never hurried, and nobody leaves the yard alone. It applies at the end of the week too. Before the long weekend drive, check that your partner's paperwork is closed out, his trailer is squared away, and you both know where you're headed Monday.

One box left to win. Every stop this week still got logged as 'discussed', never 'utilized'. The stops are real and the notes are getting good; the box just hasn't caught up. Today's challenge: if you stop a job, tick 'Stop work authority utilized' and write the scene. Be the first name on the board for it.

Finish clean before you go home: forms closed, readings written with numbers, who-was-told never blank, the trailer ready for the next crew. The week isn't over at the last job. It's over when the paperwork is done and everybody's home safe.

scenarios.title: Read It Out Loud — Then Match It
scenarios.body: Jacob, read Bryan's 9:38 note to the circle, slow. Then ask: what did it tell you? You know where he was, what time it was, what the reading was, what he did, how long he waited and how it ended. Nobody has to call him to understand that job. Now go around: everyone picks the job they're most likely to stop today and says the note they'd write. Match Bryan's. Time, reading, the stop, what you did, the recheck, how it ended. If you can say it out loud this morning, you'll write it right this afternoon.

questions: What's one thing you did differently this week because of the Stop Work talks?
Bobby changed the tool instead of skipping the control. Where else on our jobs is there a 'brass hammer' answer, a safer way to finish without bypassing anything?
What's the one item you'll double-check before you leave location today so the week ends clean?
Jacob's closing question for the week: what did the field teach us this week that the breakroom should know?
specialFocus.nonNegotiable: Finish the way we started: make the call, paint the scene, tick the box, and close every form before the truck heads home. Excellence isn't one big moment. It's this week's notes, done right, every job.
